subject: Sylphix dedicated sizing: token velocity, SLO fit and headroom
messages:
From: Alex Tucker <alex.tucker@sylphix.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@sylphix.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Initial workload profile + ask for dedicated sizing

Hi Mina / Marcus / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this. We27re evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a production rollout and need an initial sizing and SLA-fit memo to help our procurement + infra teams. Attaching a CSV with representative traffic traces (sylphix_workload_profile.csv). High-level notes:

- Model: fine-tuned Llama-2-style 70B variant (quantized 8-bit)
- Typical request: 1-3 turns; average prompt tokens ~120; average generation target ~220 tokens
- Expected steady-state peak: ~6k rps at 50% multi-turn; token-per-second estimate: we put a placeholder ~1.1M tokens/sec peak but want Redwood27s take
- p95 latency target: 300ms for streaming use-case; 99th target: 600ms
- Geo: primarily us-west with failover to us-east

Can you confirm a tokens/sec -> GPU mapping, suggested slab sizes (committed GPU counts), and what headroom we should budget for burst vs sustained periods? Also any immediate ops concerns (cold starts, KV cache warmup) to flag for procurement.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Tucker
Head of Infrastructure, Sylphix.ai
(attachments: sylphix_workload_profile.csv)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tucker <alex.tucker@sylphix.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial workload profile + ask for dedicated sizing

Alex - thanks for the trace and baseline. We'll run a few quick passes to estimate tokens/sec -> GPU, but a couple clarifying q's before we finalize numbers:

- When you say "50% multi-turn" is that 50% of sessions have 2+ turns, or 50% of requests contain conversational context appended?
- Do you expect a high fraction of short (few-token) tool calls vs long generations? That changes batching effectiveness.
- Any SLO tiers? Is p95=300ms a hard commitment or a target for the beta?

Quick note on approach:
- We'll profile the traces against two runtime profiles: 1) low-latency streaming (per-token flush) and 2) batched high-throughput (best-effort latency).
- We'll provide three slab options (small/medium/large) with tokens/sec, GPU-equivalent counts, estimated p95 under typical mix, and recommended headroom (percent over baseline).

Marcus/ Priyom - assigning compute mapping and headroom calc. Prefer to get a first-pass spreadsheet by EOD Monday and a short deck for your procurement thread.

Mina
Mina Haddad
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial workload profile + ask for dedicated sizing

Mina/Team - I ran a quick capacity model against the attached trace and our 70B quantized perf numbers. Key bullets:

- Measured single-GPU steady-state (A100-equivalent, quantized kernels, typical seq=340 tokens total) ~= 85 tokens/sec for low-latency streaming path; with aggressive batching we can push ~420 tokens/sec on the same SKU.
- Sylphix peak token target from Alex (~1.1M tokens/sec) maps to:
  - Streaming-only: ~12,900 A100-equivalents (not realistic for Dedicated)
  - Hybrid (hot-path streaming + batched background): ~2,700 A100-equivalents if most requests can be batched 4x
- Practical slab proposals (assuming 80% availability / redundancy and 30% headroom for traffic growth):
  - Small slab (pilot): 48 GPUs -> ~20k tokens/sec (batched), p95 estimate ~380ms streaming (small batch), good for trials
  - Medium slab (initial prod): 192 GPUs -> ~80k tokens/sec (batched), p95 ~320ms with prefix caching and per-route batching policies
  - Large slab (enterprise): 768 GPUs -> ~320k tokens/sec (batched), p95 ~300ms with aggressive caching + model variants fallback

Notes on headroom and ops:
- Cold KV-cache warmup can add ~30-90s of degraded p95 for the first heavy warmup; we recommend gradual ramp + prewarmed prefix cache for critical flows.
- Quantization variance: some requests (long generations) will push memory/KV pressure; recommend per-route quantization profiles and an overflow fallback to a higher-memory SKU.
- Burst strategy: use cross-region failover + short token-throttling (token leaky-bucket) to protect p95 for critical endpoints.

I've dropped a short matrix in sla_matrix.xlsx with assumptions and formulas. Priyom, please sanity-check the GPU equivalencies and the batching multipliers I used.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Inference Performance, Redwood Inference
(attachments: sla_matrix.xlsx)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tucker <alex.tucker@sylphix.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@sylphix.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial workload profile + ask for dedicated sizing

Alex / Jordan - pulling Marcus27 numbers together into a concise proposal and next steps below. Attaching a draft proposal (proposal-draft.pdf) and the spreadsheet we referenced.

Proposal summary (high level):
- Recommended initial commit: Medium slab (192 GPUs) to cover ~80k tokens/sec batched, expected to meet p95 ~320ms with caching and per-route batching. This gives Sylphix a conservative runway for initial production and buying time to optimize batching and cache footprints.

Burst & headroom plan:
- Enable a burst reserve (non-committed pool) sized at additional ~25% of committed GPUs for short spikes.
- Ops playbook: prewarm critical prefixes nightly, enable KV cache persistence for prioritized routes, set a token-throttle on non-critical endpoints during sustained peaks.

Mutual action plan:
1) Procurement signs LOI for medium slab; Redwood provides exact SKU list and region mapping (ETA 3 business days).
2) We run a 2-week pilot with realistic traffic (you provide replay) and collect p95/p99 telemetry; iterate batching/caching configs.
3) After pilot, commit to sustained slab or move to large slab depending on token growth.

Open items for Sylphix: provide a 48-hour example traffic replay (we27ll use it for pilot warmup) and flag any hard SLO commitments. If p95=300ms is non-negotiable, we should model that separately (likely requires the large slab + edge caches).

If you27re good with this, I27ll route a short procurement-ready one-pager and the SKU list to Jordan and your procurement lead.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
(attachments: proposal-draft.pdf)
